scenes.narration: Your iron *clicks* while you're ironing. So what's actually clicking in there?

scenes.visual: clean side cutaway illustration of a clothes iron cut open: the flat metal soleplate at the bottom, and just above it a small thin metal strip made of two layers fixed at one end, the strip glowing bright red-orange as the brightest thing in the frame, the iron body cool grey-blue, the cutaway large and centred in the lower two-thirds of the frame, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: No chip in there. Just a little metal *strip* that bends when it's hot. Stay for the dial bit.

scenes.narration: See, that strip is two metals stuck together, like brass and iron. Heat both, and they *grow*. But not equally...
scenes.headline: STEP 1/3: TWO *METALS*

scenes.visual: close-up illustration of two hands holding a glass jar with a stuck steel lid under a running kitchen tap, warm water pouring over the lid, the steel lid glowing bright yellow-orange as the brightest thing in the frame, steam rising gently, simple Indian kitchen sink, the jar large in the lower two-thirds of the frame, plain cool navy-blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: Ever run hot water on a stuck jar lid? Hot metal grows, so it *loosens*. Now glue two that grow differently...
scenes.headline: LIKE A *JAR LID*

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the strip rests on a contact, current runs to the heater, the number climbs, the strip curls up off the contact, CLICK, power off
scenes.narration: Brass grows more, but it's stuck to the iron. So the strip *curls* up, off the contact. <short pause> Click. Power off.
scenes.headline: STEP 2/3: IT *CURLS*

scenes.visual: warm illustration of a smiling young Indian man ironing a white kurta on an ironing board, seen from the side, his face just above the iron, the iron and its small indicator light the brightest thing in the frame in glowing red-orange, cool blue room background, the man and iron large in the middle of the frame, nothing important in the bottom third, plain cool blue background, no text or logos
scenes.narration: But here's the weird part. That click isn't a one-off. It happens *again*... and again.
scenes.headline: AGAIN AND *AGAIN*?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: the strip curls and flattens again and again, HEAT OFF, HEAT ON, CLICK each time, the temperature number wobbles around one value
scenes.narration: It cools a little, the strip *straightens*, touches the contact... click, heat's back on. Off, on, off.
scenes.headline: STEP 3/3: ON, *OFF*, ON

scenes.narration: And the dial? <short pause> It sets how far the strip must *bend* before it cuts the power. Next time it clicks, you'll know.
scenes.headline: THE *DIAL* TRICK

youtube.title: Why does my iron click? It's a bending metal strip #shorts
youtube.description:
Why does my iron click? There's no chip deciding it. Inside most irons is a thermostat: a bimetallic strip, two metals like brass and iron stuck together. When it gets hot, brass grows more than iron, so the strip curls and lifts off a contact. Click, the heater switches off. As it cools, the strip straightens, touches the contact again, and click, the heat's back on. That's how an iron thermostat works, and the dial just sets how far the strip has to bend before it cuts the power.
